summary: Adds a database migration that permanently lowercases existing mixed-case usernames (accounts made before 3.2, which could no longer log in because login now lowercases the typed name), renaming soft-deleted accounts that would clash; live accounts whose lowercase name collides with another account are left unchanged. Plus tests and a doc-comment tweak.

statements.why: The data rewrite is intended and guarded against collisions (migration.sql:2-24); no security/money problem. But the card says nothing about the user-data change.

statements.text: Apply prisma/migrations/24_lowercase_username to your live database before the new code goes live (`npx prisma migrate deploy`), or the parts that use it will fail.
statements.why: No code depends on this migration, so nothing 'fails' without it; without it, old mixed-case accounts simply stay locked out. Umami's build and docker start already run `prisma migrate deploy` (scripts/check-db.js:76).

misses.what: Existing usernames with capital letters are permanently changed to lowercase; those users (locked out since 3.2) can log in again, and their username will show in lowercase.
Accounts whose lowercase name collides with another account are skipped and stay unable to log in; deleted accounts with clashing names get renamed with a suffix.
